 | 4 | 2 | 8 | 9 | 6 | 3 | 1 | 7 | 5 |

2. Each of the three $3\times3$ blocks contains 9 different numbers. This means each block contains all numbers from 1 to 9 exactly once.

The number of ways to fill the first $3\times3$ block (cells $(1,1)$ to $(3,3)$) is the number of ways to assign numbers to these 9 cells such that each number from 1 to 9 appears exactly once. This is simply $9!$.
